items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: And Spec Red, the great piano player from DesMoines Iowa, had a drummer and a bass player and a saxophone player from Kansas City, a wonderful quartet. And they allowed me to come in and sit in and play with them all night on Tuesday.

ctx.x: And when was it that you really felt that you could become a professional musician?

Well I was very fortunate, they allowed me to join the union in Moline, Illinois when I was fourteen years old. However, in order to play the gigs at that time, you had to play in a little beer joint you know, I had to be accompanied by a grown up. They had to get me there, help me set up the drums and sit there and make sure I didn’t indulge in alcohol, and played the gig, and then he got me back home. But that was great experience because one of the greatest things that happened to me on every Tuesday night in…
That was a perfect education at that point in your career then.
